A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AReaL research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite reformatting and added material.

before.justification: v3 reports original AReaL training and evaluation results, including reasoning accuracy, training throughput, scaling measurements, and algorithmic and system ablations in Tables 1–2, Figures 4–7, and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains the original empirical results and adds coding evaluations, Llama-8B experiments, and small-scale PPO and RLOO staleness studies in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The proposed architecture, staleness-control rule, decoupled PPO objective, interruptible generation, and dynamic batching algorithm remain unchanged. Appendix C.4 introduces RLOO as an experimental alternative without revising the specified AReaL procedure.

E1.justification: v4 Table 5 adds Codeforces and CodeContests evaluations for the retained 14B and 32B coding models. Existing mathematical benchmarks and LiveCodeBench coverage remain. The Llama and smaller-cluster experiments concern configurations within the existing math tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix C.4 and Table 8 newly evaluate RLOO and explicitly compare its asynchronous-training tolerance with PPO. Existing verl, DeepScaleR, DeepCoder, and synchronous AReaL comparisons remain; the added coding benchmarks retain the existing comparator set.

E3.justification: Original experimental settings remain unchanged. Appendix C.2 adds Llama-8B runs using the Qwen-7B configuration with staleness 4 and 8. C.3–C.4 introduce 8-GPU, 8k-context experiments, with C.3 specifying batch size 64×16. These settings apply to added experiments, rather than revisions of earlier runs.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2–C.4 substantially extends the generalization and sensitivity analyses: it tests another model family, examines the staleness-throughput trade-off under a small computational budget, and investigates dependence on the RL algorithm through RLOO. The original staleness, interruptibility, and dynamic-batching ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Table 3 already specifies random seed 1. v4 Appendix A explicitly extends this disclosure across all experiments, and checklist item 7 newly states that results use a single trial and that end-to-end error bars were omitted because of cost. No additional runs or new uncertainty estimates are established.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1, 2, and 4 and plotted results are unchanged, but Tables 5–8 substantially expand the reported evidence. New CodeContests scores for asynchronous versus synchronous AReaL are 35.9 versus 37.0 at 14B and 36.5 versus 36.3 at 32B. Table 6 adds Llama-8B AIME24 scores of 58.4 and 57.2 at staleness 4 and 8, versus 50.4 for its base model. Tables 7–8 add small-scale accuracy and throughput sweeps.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Equations 1–5, and Proposition 1 retain their substance. The same proof moves from Appendix C to Appendix D; the added experiments introduce no new theorem, assumption, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about asynchronous training, controlled staleness, scalability, and up to 2.77× training speedup with comparable accuracy. New appendix evidence does not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly interprets results as supporting generalization across model families, similar staleness trade-offs with fewer GPUs, and slightly greater asynchronous tolerance for RLOO. It also proposes studying REINFORCE-like and other off-policy algorithms. Existing limitations concerning device allocation and untested multi-turn or agentic scenarios are retained.

D1.justification: v4 documents configurations for the new Llama and small-scale experiments, including configuration matching, GPU count, context length, and batch size. Checklist item 5 additionally states that code is included in supplementary material. The existing repository link, Table 3 hyperparameters, and backend-version disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 64 references and substantive related-work discussion are retained. Positioning relative to asynchronous RL, partial rollouts, StreamRL, and synchronous LLM training systems is unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains unchanged. v4 adds a checklist and reproducibility section, subdivides Additional Results, reverses the system-ablation discussion order, and updates affiliation, funding, and conference text. The Related Work heading becomes the malformed literal text 'sectionRelated Work', with subsequent sections renumbered.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 5–8 and enlarges existing Tables 1–2. The original system-ablation Figures 6 and 7 become larger panels in v4 Figure 6, retaining their plotted content. Appendix tables and the proof are relocated and reflowed; the other diagrams and plots remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The additional coding, Llama-8B, and small-cluster studies provide useful evidence about applicability, while the explicit single-trial disclosure improves transparency. These gains are limited by missing uncertainty estimates and sparse details for some new evaluations; additional coding comparisons also show mixed outcomes. The malformed Related Work heading is a small presentation regression, outweighed by the broader empirical support.
